q01: Guideline v4.8 §1.6.1(e), p15: annual turnover or revenue of less than RM3,000,000.
q02: Based on §1.6.1(e), a business that started in 2024 with RM2,000,000 turnover is below the threshold. The answer depends on the §1.6.10 carve-outs (p17): if there is a non-individual shareholder, holding company, or related company at RM3,000,000, the exemption is removed. If that information is not provided, the correct response is to ask for it rather than give a date.
q03: If your business started in 2024 and has turnover below RM3,000,000, you are exempt from issuing e-Invoice under §1.6.1(e) (p.15), unless a §1.6.10 carve-out applies. In that case, there is no implementation date.
q04: No. Under Specific Guideline §3.7.2, Table 3.6, row 7 (p.33), any single transaction exceeding RM10,000 must have its own e-Invoice, effective 1 January 2026. A RM12,000 sale exceeds RM10,000, so it cannot be consolidated.
q05: Table 3.6 row 7 states "exceeding RM10,000". Therefore, a sale of exactly RM10,000 does not exceed RM10,000 and may still be consolidated.
q06: The Special Voluntary Disclosure Programme (SVDP) for e-Invoice runs from 7 July 2026 until 31 December 2027.
q07: A self-billed e-Invoice is required for payments to agents, dealers, or distributors; goods or services from foreign suppliers; and profit distribution, among others, as stated in Specific Guideline §8.3, p. 63.
q08: Guideline Appendix 1, pp. 44-52: the e-Invoice mandatory fields are the 27 fields listed in data/rules/invoice_fields.json.
q10: Under Section 120(1)(d) of the Income Tax Act 1967, the penalty for not issuing an e-Invoice is a fine of not less than RM200 and not more than RM20,000, or imprisonment not exceeding 6 months, or both, for each non-compliance.
q11: No. An e-Invoice, including a self-billed e-Invoice, is not required for employment income under Guideline §1.6.7(a), p16, regardless of the employer’s own e-Invoice obligation.
q12: An e-Invoice is not required for a distribution of dividend in the specific circumstances in Guideline §1.6.7(d) (p.16), which cross-refers to Specific Guideline Section 11. The relevant circumstances are §11.1.2 (payers exempt from issuing) and §11.1.4 (dividends in scope). Outside those circumstances, §8.3(c) requires a self-billed e-Invoice for profit distribution.
q13: No. Zakat payments do not require an e-Invoice.
q14: No. Under Guideline §1.6.5 (p. 16), the exemption in Section 1.6.1 applies only to the specified persons. Any entities owned by those persons are still required to implement e-Invoice in accordance with the e-Invoice implementation timeline in Section 1.5. The exemption is not inherited; the entity only retains its own Section 1.6.1(e) turnover exemption, if applicable.
q15: No. Under v4.8 §1.6.1(e), businesses with annual turnover below RM3,000,000 are exempt, so a company with RM1,500,000 turnover and no corporate shareholder, holding company, or related company is not required to issue e-Invoices. The §1.6.10 carve-out does not apply.
q16: Guideline Appendix 1, p44: Buyer's TIN (field 4) is mandatory and is absent from this invoice.
q17: The corpus does not contain information on the corporate income tax rate for SMEs in Malaysia.
q18: No. SST returns are a Royal Malaysian Customs matter and are not covered in the e-Invoice Guideline, Specific Guideline, or FAQ.
q19: Guideline §1.5 Table 1.1, p12: businesses with FY2022 audited turnover of more than RM25 million and up to RM100 million are in Phase 2, with an implementation date of 1 January 2025. The table is keyed on FY2022 turnover, not current turnover (§1.5, p13).
q20: Specific Guideline §3.7.2, Table 3.6 (pp. 32–33): a consolidated e-Invoice is not allowed for sale of motor vehicles, flight tickets and private charter, construction contracts, betting and gaming pay-outs, and payments to agents/dealers/distributors. From 1 January 2026, this also includes electricity and telecommunication.
